subject: general
question: Which one of the following is the second highest peak in Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**K2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **K2** is the** world's second-highest mountain**, at 8,611 metres (28,251 feet) above sea level, after **Mount Everest **(at 8,849 metres (29,032 feet)).
 
• It is located in the **Karakoram range,** partially in Pakistan-administered Kashmir's Gilgit-Baltistan area and partially in a China-administered Kashmir region included in the Taxkorgan Tajik Autonomous County of Xinjiang.
 
• After George Bell, a climber on the 1953 American expedition, informed reporters, "It's a savage peak that attempts to kill you," K2 became known as the Savage Mountain.
 
• The mountaineering achievement was completed by a team of Nepalese climbers led by Nirmal Purja and Mingma Gyalje Sherpa in January 2021, making K2 the final eight-thousander to be summited in the winter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **At 8,485 metres, Makalu **is the** world's fifth-highest peak**. It is 19 kilometres southeast of Mount Everest in the Mahalangur Himalayas, on the boundary between Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China. Makalu, one of the eight-thousanders, is a solitary summit with a four-sided pyramid shape.
 
• **Mount Everest,** located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas, is the world's highest mountain above sea level.
 
• **Dhaulagiri, **at 8,167 metres above sea level, is the world's seventh-tallest mountain and the highest mountain within a single country's borders. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Himalayas **are an Asian mountain range that separates the Indian subcontinent's lowlands from the **Tibetan Plateau**.
 
• The range contains some of the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain.
 
• In the Himalayas, there are over 100 peaks that are higher than 7,200 metres (23,600 feet).
 
• The tallest peak outside of Asia (Aconcagua in the Andes) stands at 6,961 metres (22,838 feet).
